```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE,comment="#>",fig.width=6,fig.height=4)
library(gof)
has_ordinal <- requireNamespace("ordinal",quietly=TRUE) && requireNamespace("numDeriv",quietly=TRUE)
```

## Model and sampling unit

`cumres.clmm()` checks marginal cumulative-category residuals from a fitted
`ordinal::clmm` model. It accepts a single grouping factor or a nesting chain,
including random slopes, the five cumulative links and the four threshold
structures supported by `clmm`. Independent units are the top-level clusters.
More rows within a cluster do not create more independent multiplier draws.
Crossed and non-chain random effects are rejected.

`lava` remains a required package for existing model adapters. The optional
`ordinal` and `numDeriv` packages are needed only for the mixed-model path.

```{r wine, eval=has_ordinal}
data("wine",package="ordinal")
fit <- ordinal::clmm(rating~temp+contact+(1|judge),data=wine)
set.seed(1401)
# Nine judges is a small-cluster example; retain its warning in an analysis.
diagnostic <- suppressWarnings(cumres(fit,variable="tempwarm",R=99,plots=5))
as.data.frame(diagnostic)[c("variable","test","p.value","n","n_rows","unit")]
plot(diagnostic)
```

The wine data illustrate the interface, not a well-calibrated large-cluster
analysis. The method warns below 30 clusters and refuses fits with no more
clusters than corrected parameters. Inspect all warnings and numerical checks
before interpreting the diagnostic.

## What is diagnosed

For each row and cumulative cutpoint, the residual is the weighted indicator
of the observed category being at or below that cutpoint, minus its weighted
marginal probability. Probabilities integrate over the Gaussian random effects;
they do not condition on estimated random effects. Each top-level cluster gets
one shared normal multiplier. A score/information correction accounts for
estimated thresholds, fixed effects and random-effect covariance parameters.

The process is scaled by `sqrt(m)/sum(weights)`. `n` reports m independent
clusters, while `n_rows` reports positive-weight rows. Weights multiply the
likelihood and residual contributions. They do not implement survey sampling
or arbitrary dependence beyond the fitted cluster structure.

The default `aggregate="omnibus"` is the Euclidean norm across cumulative
cutpoint processes. `"cutpoints"` exposes signed components; `"score"` sums
them and can miss departures that preserve the ordinal mean. These summaries
are related views of the same process, not independent replications.

## Numerical estimator and acceptance checks

The supplied fit initializes adaptive Gauss--Hermite quadrature. gof polishes
the parameters to a score root with quadrature nodes frozen at their final
adaptive locations. This is a finite-quadrature estimating equation, not an
exact integrated-likelihood calculation. A separate calculation with four
more nodes per dimension checks sensitivity. Marginal probabilities use the
probit closed form or accurate one-dimensional integration as appropriate.

```{r checks, eval=has_ordinal}
diagnostic$fit_check$shift
diagnostic$fit_check$node_check
diagnostic$fit_check$boundary
diagnostic$multiplier
```

Actual covariance boundaries, unidentifiable information, nonconvergence and
failed node checks refuse ordinary inference. A weakly estimated but interior
covariance warns and reports its smallest-eigenvalue z statistic. Parameter
shifts are always reported and warn above 0.5 standard errors; the default
does not refuse a fit merely because polishing changes the estimates.
Use `gof_clmm_control()` to set numerical controls deliberately. Altering a
control after seeing a diagnostic changes the procedure being assessed.

Formula offsets must precede random-effect terms. Some `ordinal` versions
read later offsets by model-frame position; gof detects this mismatch and
asks for a refit. An `offset=` argument is rejected because `clmm` ignores it.
The supplied model object is never modified.

## Ordering and unsupported extensions

A numeric fixed-design column or retained numeric covariate can define the
ordering. All tied values enter together. `variable="predicted"` uses the
polished fixed predictor plus offset; it is not a conditional prediction or a
BLUP. Its estimated ordering still depends on the response and fitting accuracy.
Prespecify an observed covariate when possible. BLUP/conditional orderings,
joint ordering inference and crossed-effect multipliers are not implemented.

## Calibration evidence

The protocol assesses logit models across 20, 50 and 150 independent clusters,
three or ten rows per level, and intercept, slope and nested structures.
Nested designs have three children per top-level cluster and the declared
number of rows per child. Separate cells cover all five links and five
prespecified alternatives. Confirmation uses 1,000 attempted datasets per
cell and 199 multiplier draws. Pilot and opt-in test cohorts have separate
seed rosters. Every attempted dataset remains in refusal accounting.

Reported rejection rates are **conditional on an accepted fit**. Refusal
rates, failure reasons and covariance-z strata accompany them. Exact binomial
intervals are pointwise; they are neither simultaneous guarantees nor proofs
of exact nominal size. The project criterion at m >= 50 is a 5% rejection
rate between 3% and 7.5%, with refusal below 5%. Smaller-cluster results are
descriptive. A failure of either condition must remain visible.

```{r evidence, results='asis'}
evidence_path <- system.file("extdata","clmm-calibration","summary.csv",package="gof")
if (nzchar(evidence_path)) {
  evidence <- read.csv(evidence_path)
  main <- subset(evidence,alpha==.05 & stratum=="all")
  knitr::kable(main[c("id","m","nc","structure","link","alternative","statistic",
                     "attempted","accepted","rate","lower95","upper95","refusal_rate")],
               row.names=FALSE,digits=4)
} else {
  cat("Confirmation results are not installed in this development snapshot.\n")
}
```

This is an asymptotic diagnostic. Small cluster counts, boundary behavior,
quadrature sensitivity and model misspecification can affect its behavior.
Neither passing software tests nor a successful calibration cell establishes
validity for arbitrary mixed models. Full qualification retains failed and
unresolved attempts. No independent human statistical endorsement is claimed.
